c.tagline: A living medieval maze of tanneries, madrasas and the world's oldest university.

taxi.fareNote: Fès uses red petits taxis for short in-city hops (insist on the meter, or compteur) and cream grands taxis for airport runs and longer trips. There are no international ride-hailing apps in Fès, so hail on the street or ask your riad to call one; the old medina is car-free, so taxis only reach its gates.

emergency.note: Dial 19 for police and 15 for ambulance/fire (Protection Civile). Outside cities and on highways, 177 reaches the Gendarmerie Royale.

avoid.reason: Fake guides and hassle in the medina — use licensed guides; easy to get lost

hood_desc: The vast car-free medieval old city and a UNESCO World Heritage site, often called the world's largest car-free urban area, with the Al-Qarawiyyin university-mosque, the Chouara tanneries, the Bou Inania madrasa and a maze of thousands of lanes; best for first-timers who want to sleep inside a living medieval city in a converted riad.

The 'new' Marinid-era walled city west of the old medina, holding the Royal Palace's golden gates, the Mellah (historic Jewish quarter) and the Bab Semmarine market street; quieter and more spread out than Fes el-Bali, good for history without the deepest medina crowds.

The French-built modern district of wide boulevards, the train station, international-brand hotels, bars and contemporary restaurants; suits travelers who want modern comforts, nightlife and easy transport over medieval atmosphere.

The transitional quarter just outside Bab Bou Jeloud (the Blue Gate) around the Batha Museum, packed with riads, cafes and the main medina gateway; a convenient, walkable base straddling the old and new cities.

A calm, leafy residential and administrative district in the newer city with gardens, apartment blocks and local eateries; suits longer-stay and budget travelers wanting a quieter, everyday-local feel away from the tourist core.

water.note: City tap is chlorinated, but most visitors stick to bottled.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM; red petits taxis fill the late-night gaps.
transit.note: Fès has no metro or tram; the Alsa city bus network and red petits taxis are the main transport. The old medina (Fes el-Bali) is entirely car-free, so within it you walk or hire a porter with a handcart.
transit.pay: Pay bus fares in cash to the driver (a few dirhams). Petits taxis are metered by law; insist on the compteur.

train: ONCF national rail (Fès station) to Casablanca, Rabat, Marrakech, Tangier and Oujda

transit.m: Airport bus (Line 16) to the city center / train station (~30-40 min)
Grand taxi to the medina or Ville Nouvelle (20-25 min)

tip.r: Round up or leave 5-10% at restaurants; a few dirhams for cafe staff, guides and porters is customary.
